properties.name: A scheduled check runs a repository's code against its design on the server that holds the design, not against a committed export; CI itself tests the code
properties.statement:
A repository's code shall be checked against the design that governs it by asking the server that holds the design: the registered files and their fingerprints, drift, and the open gaps at or above the project's threshold. The check runs on a schedule where the server and a credential already live (for reflow2: a nightly job on flo2.io's box, in a checkout of main, through reflow2's own client), records its findings in the design as a Verification run, and fails loudly on the same findings the gate fails on today. The committed export is not read; it retires with its gate (rule 3 of dec:idea-one-blueprint-the-store-is-the-design-and-an-export-is-a-perishable-photocopy). The repository's CI tests the code only. A repository whose design is local keeps a working gate: its server is the local one. Test results travelling the other way are req:results-from-the-code-flow-back-into-a-design-that-lives-elsewhere.
HISTORY: accepted 2026-09-27 as "CI checks the code against its design on the server", with a credential CI holds. REWORDED 2026-10-10 on Anthony's word ("agree and concur on the rewording of the CI requirement"), choosing a scheduled check on the box over a credential in a public repository's CI (dec:idea-reflow2-becomes-a-plain-code-repo-and-the-design-check-moves-to-the-box, option d). What was given up: a per-PR gate; a breaking PR is caught by the next scheduled run, on main.
